source.title: Minimum Number of Work Sessions to Finish the Tasks

teaching.hint: If you choose the tasks in one session, what remains of the problem?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Order within a session is irrelevant; the task indices form a small set that must be partitioned into capacity-valid subsets.
solution_outline.approach: Represent completed tasks by a bitmask. Precompute duration sums for subsets, then for each nonempty mask try every nonempty valid submask as one session plus the optimal count for the remaining tasks.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The DP value for a mask is the minimum sessions needed for exactly its task indices. A chosen valid submask is disjoint from its remainder and consumes one session.
solution_outline.correctness: Every feasible schedule partitions its tasks into valid session subsets. The recurrence tries each possible first subset and optimally handles the rest, so it matches the best such partition.
solution_outline.pitfall: Packing each session greedily by input order need not minimize the number of sessions.

common_wrong_turns: Treating equal-duration tasks as the same index
Assuming greedy bin packing is exact
source_fidelity_notes: Removed examples; retained task indivisibility, arbitrary order, and the small task-count bound.
